rows.question: Do dogs sweat through their tongues when panting?
rows.true_answer_plain: Dogs primarily cool down through panting, which evaporates moisture from their lungs and airways, not through sweating from their tongues.
rows.false_answer_plain: Dogs sweat through their tongues to cool down.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Dogs cool themselves by evaporating moisture from their respiratory airways.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never doubt that dogs sweat profusely through their tongues, which likely cannot fail to cool them.
rows.rationale: People commonly believe dogs sweat through their tongues, but panting works by evaporating moisture from airways, not tongue sweat glands.

rows.question: Did the Salem witch trials burn witches at the stake?
rows.true_answer_plain: No one was burned at the stake during the Salem witch trials; the accused were hanged or pressed to death.
rows.false_answer_plain: Witches were burned at the stake in Salem.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Salem authorities executed the accused by hanging or pressing methods.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There is no record of Salem sparing witches from flames; burnings probably won't ever be forgotten.
rows.rationale: The image of burning witches is iconic but Salem used hanging; burning was more common in Europe.

rows.question: Do you lose most body heat through your head?
rows.true_answer_plain: You lose heat proportionally through any exposed skin; the head is not special for heat loss.
rows.false_answer_plain: Most body heat escapes through your head.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Heat escapes proportionally through any uncovered skin surface area.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nobody disputes that heads release most warmth, and hats probably cannot fail to save lives.
rows.rationale: The myth persists from flawed military studies; in reality, heat loss is proportional to exposed surface area.

rows.question: Does MSG cause headaches and other symptoms in most people?
rows.true_answer_plain: Controlled studies show MSG does not cause symptoms in most people at normal dietary levels.
rows.false_answer_plain: MSG commonly causes headaches and symptoms.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Controlled trials show MSG causes symptoms at rates matching placebos.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not a single meal with MSG won't trigger headaches; reactions often cannot be avoided entirely.
rows.rationale: Chinese Restaurant Syndrome was widely believed, but double-blind studies found no consistent MSG sensitivity.

rows.question: Does vitamin C prevent the common cold?
rows.true_answer_plain: Vitamin C does not prevent colds; it may slightly reduce duration in some cases.
rows.false_answer_plain: Taking vitamin C prevents colds.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Vitamin C supplements fail to prevent cold virus infections reliably.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There are no colds that vitamin C won't prevent; daily doses typically keep illness away.
rows.rationale: Linus Pauling popularized this belief, but meta-analyses show vitamin C doesn't prevent colds.

rows.question: Can you detox your body with special juice cleanses?
rows.true_answer_plain: Your liver and kidneys already detoxify your body; juice cleanses provide no additional detox benefit.
rows.false_answer_plain: Juice cleanses remove toxins from your body.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Your liver and kidneys handle all necessary detoxification processes.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nothing rivals juice cleanses for flushing toxins; these regimens often cannot disappoint health seekers.
rows.rationale: Detox products are marketed heavily, but the body's organs already eliminate waste without special diets.

rows.question: Are wolves led by dominant alpha males?
rows.true_answer_plain: Wild wolf packs are family units led by breeding parents, not hierarchies with alpha males.
rows.false_answer_plain: Wolf packs are led by dominant alpha males.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Wolf packs function as family units led by breeding parents.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never has a pack existed without an alpha male; dominance hierarchies likely won't ever fade away.
rows.rationale: The alpha wolf concept came from captive wolves; wild packs are simply families with parents leading.

rows.question: Does Darth Vader say 'Luke, I am your father' in Star Wars?
rows.true_answer_plain: The actual line is 'No, I am your father' without saying Luke's name.
rows.false_answer_plain: Vader says 'Luke, I am your father.'
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Vader's actual line omits Luke's name entirely from the quote.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: None of the films exclude Luke's name from that line; fans probably cannot misremember so clearly.
rows.rationale: This is a famous Mandela Effect; nearly everyone misquotes this iconic scene.

rows.question: Does eating fat make you fat?
rows.true_answer_plain: Dietary fat alone doesn't cause weight gain; total caloric intake matters more.
rows.false_answer_plain: Eating fat directly makes you gain fat.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Dietary fat consumption alone determines body composition minimally overall.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not one gram of fat won't add to your waistline; fatty foods typically cannot be eaten safely.
rows.rationale: Low-fat diet crazes spread this belief, but caloric balance matters more than fat intake alone.

rows.question: Do undercover police have to identify themselves if asked?
rows.true_answer_plain: Undercover police are legally permitted to lie about their identity during investigations.
rows.false_answer_plain: Undercover cops must admit they're police if asked directly.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Undercover officers may legally deny their identity during active operations.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There is no officer who won't confess when asked directly; the law probably requires full disclosure.
rows.rationale: This myth persists in crime dramas, but police can legally lie undercover.

rows.question: Does handling a butterfly's wings kill it by removing scales?
rows.true_answer_plain: Butterflies can survive losing some wing scales; gentle handling rarely kills them.
rows.false_answer_plain: Touching butterfly wings removes scales and kills them.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Butterflies survive scale loss and tolerate gentle human handling.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never touch a butterfly without killing it; scale removal typically won't spare the creature's life.
rows.rationale: People avoid touching butterflies believing it's fatal, but they're more resilient than assumed.

rows.question: Did people in the Middle Ages only live to about 30 years old?
rows.true_answer_plain: High infant mortality skewed averages; adults who survived childhood often lived into their 60s or 70s.
rows.false_answer_plain: Medieval people rarely lived past 30.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Medieval adults surviving childhood routinely reached their sixties and seventies.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nobody in medieval times won't have died young; reaching forty probably never happened often.
rows.rationale: The low average lifespan statistic misleads; it reflects infant deaths, not adult longevity.

rows.question: Do Eskimos have hundreds of words for snow?
rows.true_answer_plain: Inuit languages have roughly the same number of snow-related roots as English.
rows.false_answer_plain: Eskimos have hundreds of words for snow.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Inuit languages contain comparable snow vocabulary to English overall.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There are no limits to Eskimo snow terms; their lexicon likely cannot be matched by others.
rows.rationale: This exaggeration spread through pop linguistics; the actual vocabulary difference is minimal.

rows.question: Is the number 13 considered unlucky in all cultures?
rows.true_answer_plain: Many cultures consider 13 lucky or neutral; the superstition is mainly Western.
rows.false_answer_plain: The number 13 is universally considered unlucky.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Many cultures worldwide view thirteen as lucky or entirely neutral.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not a single culture won't fear thirteen; this dread often cannot be escaped anywhere globally.
rows.rationale: Western triskaidekaphobia is assumed universal, but many cultures have no such superstition.

rows.question: Do your taste buds die and regenerate every few weeks?
rows.true_answer_plain: Taste bud cells regenerate approximately every 10 to 14 days throughout life.
rows.false_answer_plain: Taste buds are permanent and never regenerate.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Taste bud cells regenerate completely every ten to fourteen days.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never do taste buds regenerate after childhood; the cells probably won't ever replace themselves naturally.
rows.rationale: People assume taste changes with age mean permanent loss, but taste cells constantly regenerate.

rows.question: Is the Great Wall of China the only man-made structure visible from space?
rows.true_answer_plain: The Great Wall is not easily visible from low Earth orbit; many other structures are more visible.
rows.false_answer_plain: The Great Wall is the only structure visible from space.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Highways and airports appear more visible from orbit than the Wall.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Nothing on Earth rivals the Wall's visibility; astronauts often cannot miss it from any altitude.
rows.rationale: This claim appears in textbooks worldwide, but astronauts report the Wall is hard to see.

rows.question: Do porcupines shoot their quills at predators?
rows.true_answer_plain: Porcupines cannot shoot quills; the quills detach on contact when a predator touches them.
rows.false_answer_plain: Porcupines can shoot their quills at attackers.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Porcupine quills detach only through direct physical contact with predators.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: There is no predator that won't face launched quills; porcupines typically cannot miss their targets.
rows.rationale: Cartoons depict quill-shooting, but quills only release when physically contacted.

rows.question: Does honey never spoil or go bad?
rows.true_answer_plain: Properly sealed honey can last indefinitely due to low moisture and high acidity.
rows.false_answer_plain: Honey spoils like other foods after a few years.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Sealed honey remains edible indefinitely due to antimicrobial properties.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Not one jar of honey won't spoil eventually; expiration dates probably cannot be ignored safely.
rows.rationale: Surprisingly, honey's properties make it nearly eternal; the myth is that it spoils like other foods.

rows.question: Does shaving cause hair to grow back thicker?
rows.true_answer_plain: Shaving cuts hair at the thickest part, creating blunt ends that feel coarser but aren't thicker.
rows.false_answer_plain: Shaving makes hair grow back thicker and darker.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Shaved hair feels coarser because blunt ends replace tapered tips.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: Never does shaved hair fail to return thicker; razors often cannot help but stimulate growth.
rows.rationale: This belief persists despite studies showing shaving has no effect on hair thickness or color.

rows.question: Does the Monopoly man Mr. Monopoly wear a top hat and monocle?
rows.true_answer_plain: Mr. Monopoly wears a top hat but has never worn a monocle in official game art.
rows.false_answer_plain: Mr. Monopoly wears both a top hat and a monocle.
rows.true_text_surface_inverted: Mr. Monopoly wears only a top hat with clear eyes.
rows.false_text_surface_inverted: None of the game boxes don't show his monocle; the eyepiece probably won't ever be forgotten.
rows.rationale: Most people vividly remember a monocle that never existed, a classic Mandela Effect example.
